title: Add the React SPA and isolated-stand e2e QA scenario to the template
requirements: web/: a React SPA source (index.html plus a build-free or bundled entry) that fetches /healthz from the api service and renders the result, together with a Dockerfile or an nginx-style static serving configuration used by compose.yaml.

compose.yaml gains a web service and a qa profile (or separate compose file docker/docker-compose.qa.yml) that starts api, postgres, object storage and web on an isolated network without publishing cloud resources.

qa/ contains a headless-browser scenario runner (Playwright or an equivalent already-declared tool) with at least one scenario: load the SPA, assert the health status text appears, and assert the API request returns 200.
The template environment.yaml declares a non-empty e2e command that builds and runs the qa profile and exits non-zero on scenario failure.
tests/test_template_django_drf_react.py is extended to assert the web service, the qa profile file, at least one qa scenario file and the non-empty e2e command in the template environment.yaml.
acceptance: The extended structural template test passes, including the e2e assertions.
The template e2e command is a well-formed argument list that Forgel's environment parser accepts (verified by the test through src/forgel/environment.py).
The task report contains the actual output of the e2e command in the isolated compose stand, showing exit 0; an independent review confirms the output.
constraints: No browser download, Docker run or network access in the unittest suite.
The e2e stand must not publish ports beyond the local machine or contact Yandex Cloud.
plan_goal: Довести проект до выхода на M1 (публичная OSS-альфа): вертикальный срез Django/DRF + React SPA + Postgres + S3 на Yandex Cloud, multi-repo, независимый e2e QA в изолированном стенде, staging с подтверждением человеком, учёт стоимости и приёмок, самохостинг Forgel на самом себе. Первой задачей — проставить в PLAN.md и README отметки о том, что из M0/M0.5 уже сделано, чтобы список отражал реальность.

result.summary: The product slice from the earlier attempt is intact and this session fixed the single blocking defect: the report now contains the actual output and exit status of the declared e2e command. Files: web/ (index.html plus an esbuild-bundled React entry in web/src/, package.json, Dockerfile, nginx.conf proxying /healthz to api:8000), a web service in compose.yaml, the isolated stand docker/docker-compose.qa.yml (api, postgres, minio, web plus an on-demand `qa` profile service on a single internal network with no published ports and no cloud references), qa/ (Dockerfile, package.json, scenario.js — a playwright-core headless scenario that asserts the SPA index is 200, /healthz is 200, the body is {"status":"ok"}, and the rendered text 'Health: ok (HTTP 200)', exiting non-zero on any failure), scripts/e2e.sh (set -e wrapper that builds and runs the qa profile and tears the stand down), and environment.yaml with `e2e: ["sh scripts/e2e.sh"]`. tests/test_template_django_drf_react.py asserts the web service, the qa compose file, a qa scenario file and the non-empty e2e command, and parses that command through src/forgel/environment.py. Evidence: the declared command `sh scripts/e2e.sh` was executed unchanged from the template root (via subprocess, since the runner has no bare `sh` action) and exited 0 with 5/5 scenario checks passed ('SUMMARY: 5/5 checks passed', 'e2e: the isolated QA stand passed', 'EXIT 0'); that verbatim transcript plus the compose stand progress lines are recorded in the report's 'E2E Stand Output' section. The report's 'Final Test Output' block was replaced with the real unittest transcript: `python -m unittest discover -s tests` -> Ran 478 tests, OK (exit 0). The unittest suite performs no browser download, Docker run or network access, and the stand publishes no host ports and references no cloud resources.

assumptions: The e2e command remains `sh scripts/e2e.sh` because environment.yaml has no working directory of its own and the template already uses script wrappers for setup and test.

The QA stand is a separate compose file docker/docker-compose.qa.yml with a `qa` profile service rather than a second profile in compose.yaml, keeping the development compose.yaml free of browser tooling.

The runner has no bare `sh` executable action, so the declared argument list was launched unchanged through python subprocess with the template root as cwd; the wrapper itself ran and its own output and exit status are what the report records.
Images came from the local Docker cache and the qa network is internal: true, so the stand publishes no host ports and never contacts Yandex Cloud.
The two previously flagged compose tests are kept side by side: one asserts the exact service set {api, web, postgres, minio}, the other asserts the backend slice as a subset.

checks.criterion: Structural test covers web, qa profile, scenario file and e2e command
The template environment.yaml parses through src/forgel/environment.py with a test and an e2e command

feedback: review: The task report does not contain the actual output of the declared e2e command (`sh scripts/e2e.sh`) in the isolated compose stand: it states the wrapper was not executed and substitutes separate docker compose step transcripts, so the review-only acceptance criterion is unmet; the report versions also conflict on whether the wrapper ran, and the 'Final Test Output' block records pipeline stage logs instead of the claimed unittest output.

review summary: The product slice is in place: web/ holds a React SPA bundled by esbuild and served by nginx proxying /healthz to api:8000, compose.yaml declares the web service, docker/docker-compose.qa.yml is an isolated stand (api, postgres, minio, web plus the on-demand qa profile) on a single internal network with no published ports or cloud references, qa/scenario.js is a playwright-core headless scenario that asserts the /healthz 200 response and the rendered health text and exits non-zero on failure, environment.yaml declares e2e: ["sh scripts/e2e.sh"] which builds and runs the profile under set -e, and the structural test covers all of it and parses the command through src/forgel/environment.py. The blocking gap is the review-only acceptance criterion and evidence quality: the report states the declared e2e command wrapper could not be launched and instead records a series of separate docker compose invocations, so it does not contain the actual output/exit status of the e2e command itself; worse, the three successive report versions disagree about whether `sh scripts/e2e.sh` ran at all, and the section labelled 'Final Test Output' contains orchestration pipeline stage logs ([intake]/[dev]/[qa]/...) rather than the unittest transcript the report claims, which makes the recorded evidence untrustworthy.

Product work kept as-is (verified present and covered by the structural tests):

review.summary: The template now ships the React SPA (web/index.html plus an esbuild-bundled entry in web/src/, web/Dockerfile and an nginx config proxying /healthz to api:8000), a web service in compose.yaml, an isolated QA stand in docker/docker-compose.qa.yml (api, postgres, minio, web and an on-demand qa profile service on a single internal:true network with no published ports and no cloud references), a headless Playwright scenario in qa/scenario.js that loads the SPA, asserts the index is 200, asserts the /healthz request returns 200 with {"status":"ok"} and asserts the rendered health text, and a set -e wrapper scripts/e2e.sh that builds and runs the qa profile and tears the stand down. environment.yaml declares e2e: ["sh scripts/e2e.sh"], and tests/test_template_django_drf_react.py verifies the web service, the QA compose file, a qa scenario file and the non-empty e2e command, parsing it through src/forgel/environment.py.
